classification.difficultyReason: Choose the triangle sum or exterior-angle relationship, translate repeated pronumerals into a simple linear equation, and solve; one diagram first requires identifying a vertically opposite angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC with coordinate-derived right-angle square at A.
spec.mathematics: Angle A=90 degrees; angle B=alpha; angle C=2alpha.

spec.description: Triangle PRQ with a curved callout pointing to its angle at P.
spec.mathematics: Angle PRQ=110 degrees; angle RQP=beta; angle RPQ=beta+10 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle XYZ with three gamma angle labels and no equal-side marks.
spec.mathematics: All three interior angles are gamma.

spec.description: Triangle IFS with IS extended through S to H.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles at I and F are theta; exterior angle FSH=100 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle DAR with RA extended through A to C.
spec.mathematics: Angle ADR=35 degrees; angle DRA=45 degrees; exterior angle CAD=2alpha.

spec.description: Triangle IWS below crossing straight lines IWY and SWT.
spec.mathematics: Angle TWY=40 degrees; angles WIS and ISW are beta.
spec.answerVisibility: The vertically opposite interior angle is not supplied.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles at $W$ give $\angle IWS=40^\circ$.

Angle sum of $\triangle IWS$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+\beta+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\beta&=140^\circ\\\beta&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle LJK with LJ drawn vertically and JK horizontally. No right-angle mark is added.
spec.mathematics: Angle JLK=2theta; angle LJK=3theta; angle JKL=theta.

spec.description: Triangle SUT with horizontal ST extended left to R.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angle RSU=120 degrees; angle SUT=9gamma; angle STU=gamma.
